classification.difficultyReason: Combines tangent and normal equations with axis intercepts, a sketch and a triangle-area calculation.

content.prompt: The tangent and normal to the cubic $f(x)=x^3$ at the point $U(1,1)$ meet the $y$-axis at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. Sketch the situation and find the equations of the tangent and normal. Find the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$, and the area of $\triangle QUP$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2\\m_{\mathrm{tangent}}&=f'(1)=3\\m_{\mathrm{normal}}&=-\frac13\end{align*}$$
Tangent through $U(1,1)$:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=3(x-1)\\y&=3x-2\end{align*}$$
Normal through $U(1,1)$:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=-\frac13(x-1)\\y&=-\frac{x}{3}+\frac43\end{align*}$$
At the $y$-axis, $x=0$, giving $P(0,-2)$ and $Q\left(0,\frac43\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}PQ&=\frac43-(-2)\\PQ&=\frac{10}{3}\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular distance from $U(1,1)$ to the $y$-axis is $1$ unit.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle QUP&=\frac12\times PQ\times1\\\text{Area of }\triangle QUP&=\frac12\times\frac{10}{3}\times1\\\text{Area of }\triangle QUP&=\frac53\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Equation-driven cubic, tangent and normal with labelled points P, Q and U; qualitative axes without numerical ticks. Source series distinctions use standard blue, red and green.
